caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 123 of 1980.
lawyer:
Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq with Mr. P.C. Guha and Mr. Manahendra Batabal, Advocate ----- For the Appellants. 
Mr. Hemayetuddin Ahmed with Mr. Menhajuddin Ahmed Khan, Advocates ----- For the Respondents.

Chan Juri Talukder & anr ------Appellants
vs.
Chingneshay Magni & ors ------Respondents
full_judgment:
9. The appellants have filed the certified copies of S.A. Khatian Nos. 154 and 190 in this Court by way of additional evidence and after hearing the learned Advocates of both the parties we have accepted the certified copies of S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190 as additional evidence on the ground that the Khatians are public documents. The learned Advocate for plaintiff respondent No.1 has submitted that the plaintiff having claimed the entire .12 decimals of land of S.A. Khatian No. 77 of plot No. 699 and he having not claimed the rest .35 decimals of land of plot No. 699 recorded in S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190, the suit does not suffer from defect of party and in support of his submission he has relied upon the case of Mir Shariatullah Vs. Abdur Rahman Bapary and others, 8 DLR (DA) 645. In the case reported in 7 P.L.R. (DA) 619 it has been held that the suit for partition is incompetent if all the co- owners are not parties to the suit as no effective decree can be passed in the absence of anyone of them. In the case reported in 10. P.L.R. (DA) 27 it has been held that the suit for partition without bringing the rest of the land of the tenancy into the hotchpotch and without impleading the other parties interested in the land, is not maintainable. In the case reported in 26 DLR (H.C.) 363 arising out of a suit for recovery of possession on declaration of title it has been held that it is one of the established principles of judicial procedure that no Court shall pass a decree which is infructuous and can be set at naught at the will of a person who has not been made a party to the suit. In the case reported in 31 DLR (AD) 218 it has been observed :- "All objections on the ground of non-Joinder or misjoinder of parties’ ought to have been taken at the earliest possible opportunity and any such objection not so taken be deemed to have been waived. Having regard to the law of procedure, it can pertinently be contended that the defendants cannot raise the question of non-joinder of parties for the first time in the court of first appeal. No Court should pass an infructuous decree. If it comes to the notice of the Court that for the absence of a party who was a necessary party in the suit, the decree which may be passed may run into jeopardy, the Court may not pass such a decree." 

 11. The proposition of law enunciated in the decisions of the above noted cases cried upon by the learned Advocate for the appellants support the view that no effective decree for partition can be passed in the absence of any necessary party and without bringing the rest of plot No. 699 in the hotchpotch that no court shall pass a decree which is infructuous and can be set at naught by a person who is a necessary party but has not been impleaded in the suit and that if it comes to the notice of the Court that for the absence of a necessary party the decree which may be passed may run into jeopardy the Court may not pass such a decree. In the instant case the recorded owners of S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190 in respect of .35 decimals of land of S.A. Plot No. 699 are surely necessary parties but they have not been impleaded in the suit and any decree' for partition that may be passed in the suit may run into jeopardy and as it may be set at naught or rendered infructuous at the will of the said recorded owners and in that view we held that a decree for partition in the absence of the said recorded owners of S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190 should not be passed' in the suit. In the present case defendant No.1 filed written statement on 22.4.74 and additional written statement on 7.8.76 but the plaint was amended on 25.8.76 incorporating a prayer for partition and as such the question of raising objection as to defect of party arose from the date of amendment of plaint on 25.8.76 after the written statement and additional written statement were filed by the defendant No.1 and so the defendant No.1 who contested the suit had no opportunity to raise objection as to defect of party and this being so the defendants can not be said to have waived the objection as to defect of party. It may be noted that the question of defect of party for non-joinder of the recorded owners of S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190 in respect of .35 decimals of land was raised in the trial court but the plaintiff did not file any application in the trial nor has she filed any in this court for amendment of the plaint for the purpose of addition of the said recorded owners in the suit nor any oral prayer on her behalf is made for remand of the case for the said purpose. The facts of the case reported in 8 DLR (DA) 645 relied upon by the learned Advocate for respondent No.1 are distinguishable from the facts of the present case. In that case a portion of a joint estate was the only property held jointly by the plaintiffs and the defendants although the defendants might be jointly interested with person other than the plaintiffs in the remaining portion of the estate but in the present case the plaintiff holds .12 decimals of land in S.A. Khatian No. 77 in plot No. 699 along with other persons who also hold .35 decimals of land in S.A. Khatians Nos. 154 and 190 in the same p IN namely 699 and yet they are not impleaded in the suit. In the light of the principles laid down in 9 P.L.R. (DA) 619, 10 P.L.R. (DA) 27, 26 DLR (H.C.) 363 and 31 D.L.R. (DA) 218 it can be held that the law laid down in 8 DLR (AD) 645 is no longer a good law. 

 From the principle enunciated in this case it is apparent that by such family arrangement there cannot be transfer of interest but there can only be arrangement for possession of the joint property amongst the heirs. In the instant case the arrangement Ext. B was made by Thanchanco for the defendants and the plaintiff was not a party to it. The plaintiff was the sale heir of the property left behind by her husband Thanchaneo under the Burmese Budhists Law of Inheritance and the defendants for whom the arrangement Ext. B was made are outsiders and not heirs and as such this arrangement is no arrangement in the eye of law and as such not admissible in evidence. It is Suited in paragraph 13 of the written statement filed by defendant No.1 that Bisudhananda Mahathero, the President of Budhya Kristi Prochar Sangha, made an award on the has is of family sculcment according to Budhist Law at the request of the District Martial Law Administrator. Defendant No. 1 Chan Juri Talukder as D.W. 1. has stated in his cross-examination that there was an award at the instance of Bisudhananda Mahathero in which the plaintiffs had consent. Thus from the pleading of defendant No. 1 and from his evidence it is clear that allegedly there was an award in respect of the property of the plaintiff at the instance of Bisudhananda Mahathero Neither the original of the alleged award nor the certified copy thereof has been filed in Court by the defendants. A true copy of the alleged award has only been filed. Mr. Hemayetuddin Ahmed the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 has submitted that the original of the alleged award having not been filed in Court the question of consideration of the allegged award does not arise. It is perfectly corrects say that the original of the alleged award having no been filed in Court the alleged award cannot be can sidered. The alleged award is again a non-testamentary instrument which purports or operate to create, declare, assign, limit or extinguish any right, title or interest of the value of Tk. 100/- or upwards to or in immovable property as mentioned in section 17(1)(b) of the Registration Act and as such it is compulsorily registrable and the alleged award having not been registered it is not enforceable in law under section 49 of the Registration Act. Finding difficulty the learned Advocate for the appellant has sought to argue that it is not an award but it is a family arrangement and that the plaintiff through her father gave consent to it and so it is binding on her. The learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1 in reply has argued that in view of his pleading and evidence that there was an award as noted above the defendant No. 1 cannot now turn round and say that it is not an award but is a family arrangement. He has further argued that even assuming for the sake of argument that it is a family arrangement then also it can be said without any fear of contradiction that it is not a family arrangement in the eye of law as plaintiff was not a consenting party to the alleged family arrangement. That the plaintiff was not a consenting party to the alleged family arrangement has been proved by D.W. 3 who has stated in his cross-examination that “বাদিনীকে কিছুই জিজ্ঞাসা করে নাই। সে সেখানে ছিল না।”
